correctness.rationale: The involution Q^rho(x)=(-1)^deg Q Q(1-x) preserves irreducibility, positive leading coefficient, degree and normalized root-counting measures. It induces A_{mu^rho,c^rho}(z)=A_{mu,c}(1-z), permutes each G_i exactly, fixes B and infinity value, so V is reflection invariant. V is jointly concave as minimum/infimum of affine functions of the probability measure mu and nonnegative c on B<=1; averaging with reflected data preserves feasibility and cannot lower V. For symmetric mu, the identity (x-t)(1-x-t)=w(x)-w(t) proves U_mu(x)=1/2 U_{w_*mu}(w(x)), yielding half-domain and one G per reflection orbit. To extend a nonclosed library with a zero-weight reflected factor, the new G_i equals the earlier off-library resultant bound and cannot undercut the original continuum/infinity minimum: this requires the additional case in Giraudin Theorem 7, not a bare assertion. Own symbolic rational w identity and nonsingular numerical G reflection calculations corroborated; all-library proof is analytic.

value.rationale: Theorem 7’s divisibility penalties are precisely the nontrivial obstruction to transferring a symmetry shortcut from upper to lower certificates. The result proves those penalties respect reflection, reducing a numerical search by half the interval and almost half the indexed constraints with no loss. This is a motivated reusable structural lemma for a current hard integer Chebyshev certificate problem, even though it does not itself sharpen the numerical t_Z bound.

scientific_limitations: Applies only to reflection-closed finite normalized irreducible libraries and finite-valued certificate data.
Does not determine an optimal numerical lower bound, true integer Chebyshev constant or globally sufficient finite library.
